aspects.says: A default method's call reaches invoke, and when the handler runs its body with InvocationHandler.invokeDefault, its calls on this come back through the proxy.
basis: section:A Call the Target Makes on this Never Reaches the Proxy
aspects.reason: a side note contrasting the self-call rule; the page shows no run of it beyond the reference table, and a practice would test a JDK method's contract rather than a reader's decision

aspects.says: A JDK proxy implements only the listed interfaces: it is not an instance of the target's class, so a cast to that class fails, and Proxy refuses a class; proxying a class needs a generated subclass.
basis: section:One InvocationHandler Receives Every Call on Every Method of the Proxied Interfaces

aspects.says: equals, hashCode and toString reach the handler; forwarding equals to the target makes the proxy unequal to itself, so a list can't remove it, and the handler should answer them itself.
basis: section:equals, hashCode and toString Reach the Handler Too, So the Handler Decides the Proxy's Identity

aspects.says: Proxy.newProxyInstance generates a class implementing the listed interfaces whose every method call goes to one InvocationHandler, which can serve any interface, the JDK's included.
basis: section:One InvocationHandler Receives Every Call on Every Method of the Proxied Interfaces

aspects.says: Whatever the handler does with its proxy argument goes back through invoke, so printing proxy inside the handler recurses until StackOverflowError.
basis: section:equals, hashCode and toString Reach the Handler Too, So the Handler Decides the Proxy's Identity

aspects.says: A call the target makes on this goes straight to the target and never reaches the proxy, so behaviour attached to the called method is skipped; the call must go through the proxy reference.
basis: section:A Call the Target Makes on this Never Reaches the Proxy

aspects.says: A checked exception thrown by a handler that the interface method doesn't declare reaches the caller as UndeclaredThrowableException, skipping the caller's catch; unchecked and declared exceptions pass through unchanged.
basis: section:A Checked Exception the Interface Method Doesn't Declare Reaches the Caller as UndeclaredThrowableException

aspects.says: Method.invoke wraps whatever the target throws in InvocationTargetException, so a handler that tests or rethrows the wrapper retries nothing and changes the type of every failure; it must work with getCause().
basis: section:Method.invoke Wraps Whatever the Target Throws, So the Handler Must Unwrap It
